story.head: Expect the Devils to fire from everywhere
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Washington on Oct 17. The Devils (13-6-0) lost 4-2 to Winnipeg on Tuesday, while the Capitals have won two in a row. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Capitals fourth (17th in the NHL) and the Devils second (tied for sixth).

The Capitals’ record (.625) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.562), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Devils have played better than their record (.684) says: their chances are worth about .745, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Capitals get the league’s best looks (1st), have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th) and get into a lot of chippy games (5th). As for the Devils, they draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and rarely throw hits (2nd lowest). They also throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd), so the Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Caps.

Dylan Strome (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 16 GP) leads the Capitals in scoring, and Alex Tuch (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. Jack Hughes (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 19 GP) leads the Devils in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 15 A / 19 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games.
Logan Thompson (7-4-0 / .892 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Washington, and Jake Allen (6-4-0 / .880 SV% in 10 GS) for New Jersey.
